justification: One-line Railway config change: dcp-extract cron weekly (Mon) to daily. Founder decision 2026-07-28; near-free no-op when the queue is empty; closes the up-to-6-day stuck window that tripped the watchdog by design.

break_it.scenario: Daily runs pile up Modal OCR spend on chapters that repeatedly trigger the fallback.
break_it.what_happens: A garbled chapter stuck awaiting review would be re-OCRed every day.
break_it.how: Extraction only processes needs_extraction chapters; a chapter awaiting REVIEW keeps its pending rows and the refresh replaces them, but the OCR trigger re-fires only while the source text layer stays garbled - bounded by review cadence, and the watchdog now names review-blocked chapters explicitly. Worst case a few dollars a week, visible on the Modal dashboard.
break_it.repro: Flag a garbled chapter and leave it unreviewed two days - two OCR passes.

post_merge.other_repo: Railway picks the schedule up from config-as-code on next deploy (auto-deploys on merge).
post_merge.manual_verify: Yes - Railway dcp-extract service shows Next run tomorrow instead of next Monday.
